blocks.text: AI Guard in proxy mode can inspect AI traffic that ZIA forwards without a user, including traffic from servers and other workloads, and from branches connected through Zero Trust Branch (ZTB). Previously, the proxy rejected this traffic before any policy ran, so it was neither checked nor logged.

blocks.item: Checks the signature on the header. A missing or invalid signature is rejected.
Finds the tenant from the ZIA tenant ID.
Checks that the tenant has Unauthenticated Traffic enabled. If not, the request is rejected with 401 error.
Takes the client IP from the X-Forwarded-For tag.
Checks the prompt and the response against the tenant's Unauthenticated Traffic rules.
Go to AI Guard > Tenant Settings > Security.
Under Security Settings, turn on Enable Unauthenticated Traffic.

blocks.text: This functionality is shown only to tenants in proxy mode, and only users who can update tenant settings can change it. The change is recorded in the audit log.
To add an unauthenticated traffic rule:

blocks.item: Go to AI Guard > Policy > Controls > Users.
Click Add More. The Create Policy Control window appears.
Rule Name: Enter a name for this rule such as Unauthenticated Traffic Rule.
Policy Configuration: Select the desired policy.
Under Match Criteria, click the Unauthenticated Traffic dropdown and select All Unauthenticated Traffic.
If you want to narrow down the match criteria further, you can select from LLM Provider and User Agent Type.
